So what advice would you give to someone starting out in IT who has no formal education in it but is knowledgeable enough to be running a Linux main computer?

I never had any formal education in it, either.

Start off by writing scripts. Find some annoying tasks that you do frequently and script it out. Riping of CDs/DVDs/PS games, etc. Cleaning up of old, unused kernels, updating of Blu-ray key files, the list goes on.

Find those tasks and write scripts to automate them. But, most importantly is that when you write them always ask yourself "what happens if this task fails?" There needs to be proper error checking through out the script.

For example, if you have a simple script that will make a tarball of a folder and copy it to an NFS share, there should be checks to make sure the NFS is mounted and has the right permissions. When making the copy, check to see if there's enough storage. After each command, did they return a 0 exit status? If not, can it continue anyway? If not, how should you be notified?

A good rule of thumb is that a good script should be 80% error checking and 20% actual script. It might be more like 90/10 but you get the idea.
